summary.intent: Add monitoring improvements for 'someguy' service and clean up test run artifacts from the repository.
summary.outcome: Committed monitoring changes (Alloy config scrape target and docker-compose healthcheck fix), added fixtures/files/ to e2e .gitignore, and untracked .last-run.json which had been accidentally committed before the ignore rule existed.

repo: The tests/e2e/fixtures/files/ directory is entirely runtime-generated by createTestTextFile/createTestBinaryFile helpers and should never be committed.
.last-run.json lives in tests/e2e/test-results/ and was previously tracked by git before the gitignore rule was added, requiring explicit git rm --cached.

There are two layered gitignore files: root .gitignore has 'tests/e2e/test-results/*' and tests/e2e/.gitignore has '/test-results/' — the file was tracked despite these rules because it predated them.
The project uses Grafana Alloy (alloy-config.river) for Prometheus scraping and docker-compose.staging.yml for staging environment orchestration.
c4-* prefixed files are load test artifacts from a tool called C4.

code.finding: fixtures/files/ entry was added to ignore runtime-generated test fixture files.

workflow: Files tracked by git before a gitignore rule is added remain tracked — must use 'git rm --cached' to untrack without deleting the local file.
When a gitignore rule exists at multiple levels (root and subdirectory), a previously-tracked file will still appear as modified until explicitly untracked.

friction: .last-run.json was already covered by an existing gitignore rule but remained tracked because it was committed before the rule existed, requiring a separate untrack step.
The c4-* load test artifacts were left over from a failed test run (C4's run), cluttering the working tree.
open_items: Push the chore/someguy-monitoring-improvements branch and open a PR — was deferred pending the cleanup work.
Investigate whether cleanupTestFiles helper should be deleting fixtures/files/ contents after test runs to prevent future artifact accumulation.
